solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Survey Saracens, usually taking a sample

indicators.note: taking a sample means a short run of letters is lifted out of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A pollster questions a rugby club's players, as is their habit, by sampling a few of them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking a sample' signals letters lifted from inside 'Saracens, usually', across the word gap.
explanation.definitionFit: An official count of a population is a kind of survey, so the two nouns match.

clue.text: Jack the writer's the talk of Harlem

parts.note: J is the card abbreviation for jack
the writer refers to the setter, I; the writer's here stands for the writer has, I've

explanation.surface: A literary figure called Jack is the sensation of Harlem's talk.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'the writer's' is 'has', giving I'VE, the setter's own contraction.
explanation.definitionFit: Jive was the slang of 1930s and 1940s Black American jazz culture, centred in Harlem.

clue.text: Trouble experienced over flowering plant

indicators.note: in a down clue over tells us to turn the preceding pair of words back to front

parts.note: to trouble someone is to ail them
experienced as in had, underwent

explanation.surface: Someone recounts the trouble they had with a plant in bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns AIL plus HAD back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: The garden bloom named after the botanist Dahl is one specific flowering plant.

clue.text: Focus around one literary volume

indicators.note: around means the word for focus wraps the following pieces

parts.note: a focus is a centre
one is the Roman numeral I
lit is short for literary, as in lit crit

explanation.surface: Someone is told to concentrate on a single book of literature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Volume' looks like a book alongside 'literary', but it means a quantity of liquid.
explanation.definitionFit: A hundredth of a litre is a measure of capacity, a volume.

clue.text: It's a relief map's final cut

indicators.note: final points to the closing letter of the word map

parts.note: to hew is to cut, as with an axe

explanation.surface: The finished trimming of a relief map, raised contours and all, is the final cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'relief map' is a single idea in the surface; the definition splits it after 'relief'.
explanation.definitionFit: The exclamation is uttered when tension lifts, so it expresses relief.

clue.text: Light bender in big city shortly, one near Belarus

indicators.note: in tells us the light bender sits inside the shortened city
shortly means the city word loses its last letter

parts.note: the Smoke is a nickname for London, the big city
a lens bends light

explanation.surface: A beam of light is refracted somewhere in a large city, close to Belarus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Smoke' is a British nickname for London, the big city; 'shortly' cuts its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The Russian city lies close to the Belarusian border, so it is one city near Belarus.

clue.text: As well as plugging Parisian from the rugby, managed a pop band

parts.note: du is French for from the, as a Parisian would say

indicators.note: plugging means the word for as well as fills a gap in the rugby abbreviation

parts.note: RU stands for Rugby Union
as well as means and
to run something is to manage it, so managed is ran

explanation.surface: A Parisian, as well as a rugby fan, ran a pop group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parisian from the' asks for the French word, not a person from Paris; 'plugging' signals the insertion.
explanation.definitionFit: The 1980s New Romantic group behind Rio and Hungry Like the Wolf was a pop band.

clue.text: Between old priest and hospital there's variable aid for Queen

indicators.note: between means the next pieces sit between the priest and the hospital

parts.note: Eli is the priest of the Old Testament who raised Samuel
Z is a common algebraic variable
to abet is to aid

explanation.surface: A religious charity sits between an elderly priest and a hospital, raising money for the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: ZABET goes between ELI and H.
explanation.definitionFit: Two English monarchs called Queen have borne this name, so it is a royal first name.

clue.text: Opening and middle of Shamela by Fielding, Henry

indicators.note: middle of picks the central letter of the seven-letter title

parts.note: in cricket the fielding side is the side that is out, not batting
H is the symbol for the henry, the unit of inductance

explanation.surface: The start and middle of Shamela, the parody novel by Henry Fielding.
explanation.walkthrough: Shamela is Henry Fielding's parody of Richardson's Pamela; 'Fielding, Henry' reads as the author's name but splits into two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: An opening such as the end of a river or a cave entrance is called its mouth.

clue.text: Briefly assist police force's protection at the top level

indicators.note: briefly means the word for assist is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: to assist is to help
the Met is London's Metropolitan Police; the 's is a contraction of is

explanation.surface: A short spell assisting the police force's protection of senior people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at the top level' sounds like seniority but means literally on the head.
explanation.definitionFit: Headgear worn to guard the skull is protection worn at the very top of the body.

clue.text: Dandy appearing twice in Shakespearean comedy

definitions.meaning: a dandy is a fashionable man, a toff
the comedy All's Well That Ends Well contains these five letters twice, at All's Well and Ends Well

explanation.surface: A foppish character shows up twice in one of Shakespeare's comedies.
explanation.walkthrough: In All's Well That Ends Well the letters run across 'All's Well' and again across 'Ends Well'.
explanation.definitionFit: An old informal noun for a smartly dressed, fashionable gentleman, a toff.

clue.text: What drapes one may be wringing or all wet

indicators.note: wringing means twisting, so the letters are twisted into a new order

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A towel hung up may be soaking wet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wringing' twists I (one) and ORALLWET; the surface's 'wringing wet' disguises the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A bathroom bar over which cloths are hung is the thing that drapes them.

clue.text: Derelict esplanade denies slogan with fatal consequences for Italian port?

definitions.text: slogan with fatal consequences for Italian port?

indicators.note: derelict means ruined, so the following letters are in ruins and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A rundown seafront rejects a deadly motto meant for an Italian port.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Derelict' rearranges ESPLANADEDENIES.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb about the southern Italian city urges a visit before dying, so taken literally it carries fatal consequences.

clue.text: Side with couple, united in aims where slugs have come out?

indicators.note: in tells us the side, couple and united go inside the aims

parts.note: aims are ends, goals
a cricket or football side has eleven players, XI
a couple is two
U is the abbreviation for united, as in football club names

explanation.surface: A team allied with a pair, united in their goals, as if in a garden where slugs emerged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'slugs' are bullets, not garden pests.
explanation.definitionFit: Bullets, called slugs in slang, leave the body through these injuries.

clue.text: Remarks about iron temperature burning, which could make it hard to play ball

definitions.text: which could make it hard to play ball

indicators.note: about means the word for remarks goes round the next two pieces

parts.note: remarks are says, as in he says
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
burning means hot

explanation.surface: Comments about a hot iron's temperature, which could make it hard to play.
explanation.walkthrough: In snooker and pool this stroke leaves the opponent badly placed to pot.
explanation.definitionFit: A defensive stroke in cue sports deliberately leaves the opponent no easy ball to play.

clue.text: Wood turned into a tool or vice versa

definitions.text: Wood turned into a tool or vice versa

indicators.note: into means the turned wood goes inside the word for a tool

parts.note: a tool is slang for a fool, a git

indicators.note: turned means the tree name is read backwards

parts.note: elm is a wood

explanation.surface: Carpentry turns timber into an implement, or the other way round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a tool' is the slang insult, not an implement; read whole, the clue also describes the boring tool, which is turned into wood: the vice versa.
explanation.definitionFit: The small T-handled hand tool is twisted into timber to bore holes, so the whole clue pictures it.

clue.text: Spike in movie-making involves Hawk's feature much less

indicators.note: involves means the director's surname wraps round the bird's feature

parts.note: Spike Lee is the American film director
a hawk has talons, its claws

explanation.surface: A film director's project features a hawk, though much less prominently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spike' looks like a sharp point next to a hawk's talon, but it is the film-maker Spike Lee.
explanation.definitionFit: Both phrases are idioms meaning still less, as in I can't walk, much less run.

clue.text: Dissembling king in old enchanted land

indicators.note: in places the king letter inside the old fairyland

parts.note: faery is an archaic spelling of fairyland
K is the chess abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: A deceitful king in a magic kingdom of old.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dissembling' is a noun here, the act of pretending.
explanation.definitionFit: Pretence and deception, the act of dissembling, is falseness or sham.

clue.text: Air conditioning in a coach is something to count on

indicators.note: in places the air conditioning inside the vehicle

parts.note: a coach is a bus

explanation.surface: A coach with air conditioning is something you can rely on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'count on' reads as rely on, but means literally to count with.
explanation.definitionFit: A frame of beads used for arithmetic is literally a device to count on.

clue.text: Make changes to renew trust, stopping gaffe for cop's predecessor

indicators.note: stopping means the rearranged letters plug the gap in the word for gaffe

parts.note: a boner is a blunder, a gaffe

indicators.note: make changes to means the following letters are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: Reform is needed to restore trust after a police gaffe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make changes to' signals the anagram and 'stopping' the insertion. The Bow Street Runners were London's early police force of the 1700s.
explanation.definitionFit: Members of this 18th-century London force came before modern police constables.

clue.text: Sky-god and bishop dismissed by a pope and people generally

indicators.note: dismissed by means the bishop is removed from the pope's name

parts.note: Urban was the name of several popes
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
us means people generally, as in it makes us think

explanation.surface: A sky-god and a bishop sacked by a pope, and by ordinary people.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the primordial deity of the heavens, father of the Titans, is a sky-god.

clue.text: Send to a specialist to bind back of knee joint

indicators.note: to bind means the word for send on wraps round the letter from the knee

parts.note: doctors refer patients to specialists

indicators.note: back of picks the final letter of the word knee

explanation.surface: A GP sends a patient to a specialist to strap up the back of a knee joint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'knee joint' runs together in the surface; 'joint' alone is slang for a cannabis cigarette.
explanation.definitionFit: A cannabis cigarette is called a joint in slang, as is this older word.

clue.text: Regret breaking chlorine bonds in wanton acts

indicators.note: breaking means the regret word splits the chemical letters apart

parts.note: Cl is the chemical symbol for chlorine
to regret is to rue
bonds are ties

explanation.surface: A chemist regrets breaking chlorine bonds in a reckless experiment.
explanation.definitionFit: Acts of deliberate, gratuitous harm are called cruelties.

clue.text: First person to live by mountain-dweller

parts.note: the first person singular pronoun is I
to be is to exist, to live
by as in multiplied by, written as the times sign X

explanation.surface: The first person ever to live beside a mountain dweller.
explanation.definitionFit: The wild goat lives high in the Alps and other mountain ranges.

clue.text: US dramatist sheltered from bluster about book

indicators.note: about means the sheltered word goes round the book letter

parts.note: alee means on the side sheltered from the wind

explanation.surface: An American playwright hides from noisy criticism of a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bluster' looks like ranting but is a gusting wind.
explanation.definitionFit: Edward Albee, who wrote Who's Afraid of Virginia Woolf?, was an American playwright.

clue.text: Hollow sound from water pipe

definitions.meaning: a deep resonant ringing note, as of a large bell
a pipe for smoking that draws smoke through water

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a deep ringing note and a smoking pipe with a water chamber.

clue.text: Chair historically carried dean's duff

indicators.note: duff is British slang for faulty or useless, so the letters are wrongly arranged

explanation.surface: A dean's useless old carrying chair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'duff' (British slang for broken) rearranges DEANS.
explanation.definitionFit: A sedan chair was an enclosed seat borne on poles by two carriers in the 17th and 18th centuries.

clue.text: In series, apart from its debut, see skill with words

indicators.note: in means the word for see goes inside the trimmed series
apart from its debut means the series word loses its first letter

parts.note: a series is a sequence
lo is an old word for see, as in lo and behold

explanation.surface: In a television series, see someone's way with words, except in the first episode.
explanation.walkthrough: 'apart from its debut' drops the S of SEQUENCE; LO goes into EQUENCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Fluent, persuasive speaking is a gift for language, a skill with words.
